claim: Restore testing is an AWS Backup feature that automatically and periodically evaluates whether restores will work, and monitors restore job duration.
question: What is restore testing in AWS Backup?

values.display: automated and periodic evaluation of restore viability
monitor restore job duration times

evidence.quote: Restore testing, a feature offered by AWS Backup, provides automated and periodic evaluation of restore viability, as well as the ability to monitor restore job duration times.

claim: You create a restore testing plan with a name, the test frequency and the target start time, assign the resources to include, and choose specific or random recovery points; AWS Backup infers the metadata needed for the restore.
question: How do you set up restore testing?

values.display: the frequency for your restore tests
specific or random recovery points

evidence.quote: First, you create a restore testing plan where you provide a name for your plan, the frequency for your restore tests, and the target start time. Then, you assign the resources you want to include in your plan. You then choose to include specific or random recovery points in your test. AWS Backup backup intelligently infers the metadata that will be needed for your restore job to be successful.

claim: When the scheduled time arrives AWS Backup starts restore jobs from the plan and monitors the time taken; afterwards you can use the results to show compliance, such as successful restore test scenarios or the restore job completion time.
question: What can you use restore test results for?

values.display: monitors the time taken to complete the restore
restore job completion time

evidence.quote: When the scheduled time in your plan arrives, AWS Backup starts restore jobs based on your plan and monitors the time taken to complete the restore.

After the restore test plan completes its run, you can use the results to show compliance for organizational or governance requirements such as the successful completion of restore test scenarios or the restore job completion time.

claim: Once the optional validation completes or the validation window closes, AWS Backup deletes the resources involved in the restore test, in accordance with service SLAs.
question: What happens to the restored resource after a restore test?

values.display: AWS Backup deletes the resources involved with the restore test
validation window closes

evidence.quote: Once the optional validation completes or the validation window closes, AWS Backup deletes the resources involved with the restore test, and the resources will be deleted in accordance with service SLAs.

claim: Restore testing runs restore jobs in the same way as on-demand restores and uses the same recovery points as an on-demand restore.
question: How does a restore test differ from an on-demand restore in how it restores?

values.display: runs restore jobs in the same way as on-demand restores
same recovery points

evidence.quote: Restore testing runs restore jobs in the same way as on-demand restores and uses the same recovery points (backups) as an on-demand restore.

claim: The resource types you can assign to a restore testing plan are Aurora, DocumentDB, DynamoDB, EBS, EC2, EFS, FSx (Lustre, ONTAP, OpenZFS, Windows), Neptune, RDS and S3, while any resource can be restored on demand.
question: Which resource types can a restore testing plan include?

values.display: The resource types you can assign to your testing plan include
All resources can be restored

evidence.quote: | **Resources** | The resource types you can assign to your testing plan include: Aurora, Amazon DocumentDB, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon EBS, Amazon EC2, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx (Lustre, ONTAP, OpenZFS, Windows), Amazon Neptune, Amazon RDS, and Amazon S3. | All resources can be restored. |

claim: After a restore testing job completes, the restored resource is deleted when the validation window finishes, whereas after an on-demand restore job the restored resource remains.
question: Is the resource from a restore test kept?

values.display: the restored resource is deleted after the
the restored version of the resource remains

evidence.quote: | **Results** | After the restore testing job is completed, the restored resource is deleted after the [Restore testing validation](restore-testing-validation.md) window finishes. | Once the restore job is completed, the restored version of the resource remains. |

claim: AWS Backup Audit Manager can turn on a control to confirm whether a restore test meets specified restore objectives.
question: Can Audit Manager check whether restore tests meet your restore objectives?

values.display: Can turn on a control to confirm if a restore test meets specified restore objectives
AWS Backup Audit Manager

evidence.quote: | **AWS Backup Audit Manager** | Can turn on a control to confirm if a restore test meets specified restore objectives |  |

claim: The recommended best practice for restore testing is to designate an account to be used for restore tests.
question: Which account does AWS recommend for running restore tests?

values.display: designate an account to be used for restore tests
Recommended best practice

evidence.quote: | **Account** | Recommended best practice is to designate an account to be used for restore tests | You can restore resources from an account |

claim: Resources restored by a restore testing plan that support tag-on-restore carry the awsbackup-restore-test tag; if a user removes the tag, AWS Backup cannot delete the resource at the end of the test and the user must delete it manually.
question: What happens if the restore-test tag is removed from a restored resource?

values.display: awsbackup-restore-test
AWS Backup cannot delete the resource at the end of the testing period

evidence.quote: Resources that are restored by a restore testing plan and support tag-on-restore have a tag of `awsbackup-restore-test`. If a user removes this tag, AWS Backup cannot delete the resource at the end of the testing period and the user will have to delete it manually instead.

claim: Restore testing validation is an optional event-driven check: you build a validation workflow with any EventBridge target such as Lambda and an EventBridge rule that listens for the restore job reaching COMPLETED.
question: How do you validate a restore test result automatically?

values.display: event-driven validation
any target supported by Amazon EventBridge

evidence.quote: You have the option of creating an event-driven validation that runs when a restore testing job completes.
First, create a validation workflow with any target supported by Amazon EventBridge, such as AWS Lambda.
